_partNote: Class tiles for industrial-automation-and-controls, generated 2026-08-19 with `generate-images.js parts`. Each subject was checked against this sheet's own entry list and sits in the class it illustrates: the DIN-rail controller is entry 1 in class I, the transmitter is entry 13 in class III, the servo motor is entry 17 in class IV, the light curtain is entry 22 in class V, and the operator panel is entry 27 in class VI. Class VII uses a floor-standing cabinet, which is no entry's subject, and is kept visually distinct from class I by having an enclosure and a door where class I is a bare rail. The color list is this domain's trap set: safety equipment is safety-yellow and orange, warning labels are yellow and black stripes, control cabinets are light gray with a colored backplate, and every major vendor has a signature body color. Installed tiles are the 'a' candidate for all seven classes, from the first pass, at 900px wide. The light curtain in class V came back correctly proportioned first time because the prompt gave the ratio as a number ('at least ten times taller than it is wide, like a narrow flagpole'), which is the rule learned from the rotor sail on the maritime sheet.
style: Minimalist technical illustration, the style of a precise patent drawing crossed with an isometric product sketch. Uniform-weight dark slate-gray ink linework with sparse, muted steel-blue accent shading (hex 4E7AA8) on a plain very light warm-gray background (hex F2F3F1). Three-quarter isometric view, single centered subject, generous margins. No text, no labels, no callouts, no logos, no humans, no background scenery, no drop shadows. Clean, engineered, calm. Strictly two colors plus the background: dark slate-gray line and muted steel-blue fill. The drawing must read as line art, not as a rendered solid model. Absolutely no safety yellow, no orange, no yellow-and-black hazard striping, no red or green indicator lamps, no copper, brass or gold, and no vendor signature colors of any kind, even where the real equipment would be exactly that color. Every housing, cable and label is drawn in the same two-color palette.

partPrompts.1: Three identical control modules clipped side by side on a horizontal mounting rail, seen three-quarter: each module is a slim upright rectangular block, about three times taller than it is wide, with a plain narrow front face carrying a single row of small terminal openings down one edge, and all three sit squarely on one straight horizontal rail that extends a short distance past the modules at both ends. No enclosure, no cabinet, no door, no wires, no screen, no lamps. Bold and obviously a row of blocks on a rail.
